title: [Power Display] Monitor P275MV PLUS is duplicated and disappears until reboot

judgment.rationale: The diagnostic archive ties disappearance to transient DDC capability failure while DisplayConfig still reports the monitor; persisted identities explain duplicate rows.
evidence: The report shows duplicate P275MV PLUS entries and disappearance after standby or refresh.
The diagnostic data contains the same EdidId with different DevicePath segments.
Power Display logs show repeated empty DDC capability responses for a DisplayConfig-present monitor.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the degraded-discovery and conservative deduplication design, with hardware validation.

fix_assessment.rationale: Adjacent wake and compatibility fixes do not keep a DisplayConfig-present monitor visible in normal mode.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep DDC-flaky displays visible and coalesce stale identity duplicates
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Discovery drops a monitor when capability reads are empty even though DisplayConfig sees it, while DevicePath churn leaves multiple recent persisted identities for one display.
plan: Create a degraded monitor from known-good VCP or persisted capabilities after live capability retries fail.
Keep unsupported controls disabled and retry live discovery on refresh or wake.
Coalesce only stale same-EdidId/name entries when one identity is currently discovered; never merge two simultaneously discovered monitors.
verification: A capability failure leaves one degraded monitor row visible.
A later refresh clears degraded state after live capabilities recover.
Two simultaneous identical monitors remain separate while stale DevicePath duplicates collapse.

confidence.rationale: The missing-monitor path is directly evidenced; hardware-specific wake behavior and duplicate identity policy need targeted validation.

issue_context.summary: Power Display loses a P275MV PLUS after transient DDC failure and can show duplicate persisted rows caused by changing device-path identity.
known_information: The affected monitor is P275MV PLUS with EdidId LHC907D.
The report includes screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP.
Logs record the display as active but show empty capability responses.
Related work includes wake rescan and compatibility-mode fallback changes.
inferences: DisplayConfig presence should determine whether a monitor remains listed; DDC capability readiness should determine control availability.
A current identity should win over stale same-model persisted identities.
issue_context.analysis: Separating existence from capabilities addresses disappearance without inventing unsupported controls. Conservative deduplication addresses DevicePath churn while protecting two truly simultaneous identical displays.
initial_investigation: Inspected DdcCiController, VcpDiscoveryEvidence, MonitorManager, MainViewModel monitor refresh, and MonitorSettingsRebuilder.
Reviewed related history for wake rescan, persisted VCP fallback, monitor-state locking, and abandoned handles.
Fork mirror Issue 635 contains the detailed design and adversary approval.

information_gaps.information: A reproducible P275MV PLUS wake or capability-failure trace on current main
information_gaps.why_needed: It will confirm the degraded path is sufficient for the hardware-specific failure.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce after standby or wake and add a comment containing /bugreport immediately afterward.

design.root_cause: Normal discovery drops a physical monitor when DDC capability acquisition returns no capabilities, despite QueryDisplayConfig reporting the display. Persisted monitor settings retain older DevicePath variants, so the same EdidId can appear more than once.
evidence: [Observed] The diagnostic log reports P275MV PLUS as active and records repeated empty capability responses.
[Observed] Settings contain two P275MV identities with the same EdidId but different DevicePath segments.
[Observed] Current discovery drops the monitor when capabilities remain null.
[Inferred] Cached positive capabilities can safely keep a row visible if writes remain guarded.

affected_files.purpose: Retains and rebuilds persisted monitor identities.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: A monitor with no live capability string is discarded.
implementation_steps.change: Use recent known-good VCP or persisted capabilities to construct a degraded monitor; discard only when no evidence exists or the physical handle is invalid.
implementation_steps.code_block: if (evidence.Capabilities == null && cache.TryGet(monitorId, out var cached)) evidence = FromCached(cached, degraded: true);\nif (evidence.Capabilities == null) return null;\nreturn BuildMonitorFromPhysical(evidence);
edge_cases: Never synthesize support without prior positive evidence.
Writes must still fail safely and trigger refresh.
Keep extra probing disabled in normal mode.
tests: Empty live caps plus cache yields degraded monitor.
Empty live caps without cache preserves existing discard behavior.

implementation_steps.change: Merge only stale non-current entries sharing normalized EdidId and name; preserve two current identities.
implementation_steps.code_block: candidates = retained.Where(!currentlyDiscovered || id != current);\ncoalesce(key: EdidId + normalizedName, prefer: current then newest);
edge_cases: Do not merge two simultaneously discovered identical monitors.
tests: One current plus one stale duplicate becomes one.
Two current identical monitors remain two.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: The UI removes a monitor when DDC discovery omits it.
implementation_steps.change: Retain degraded rows and show unavailable controls until refresh recovers capabilities.
edge_cases: Clear degraded state only after successful live reads.
tests: View model retains row and disables unsupported controls.

verify: Build PowerDisplay.Lib.UnitTests with tools\build\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Release -Project src\modules\powerdisplay\PowerDisplay.Lib.UnitTests\PowerDisplay.Lib.UnitTests.csproj.
Run targeted tests with vstest.console.exe using filters for DdcCiController, VcpDiscoveryEvidence, and MonitorSettingsRebuilder tests.
Reproduce standby/wake or inject an empty capability response while QueryDisplayConfig remains present; confirm a degraded row remains.
Recover DDC and refresh; confirm live capabilities replace degraded state and stale duplicate rows are not recreated.
risks: Cached capabilities can become stale; guard writes and require live success to clear degraded state.
Over-aggressive deduplication could merge identical monitors; current-discovery exclusion prevents that.
alternatives: Only enabling maximum compatibility mode leaves the default drop path.
Increasing retries improves timing but does not solve persisted duplicates or permanent transient failure.
